steps.title: Six filters in one table
notes: S_FILTERS lists every filter with its format, its file extension and two switches: per_layer for the ZIP formats and with_ramps for 3MF. The order of the table is the order in the Execute dialog.
ATU asks for the filters through the entry point declareExportFilter. The id must stay the same in every language; only the name is localized.

lines: { id: S_filter_lsr_single, name_key: 'filter_lsr_single', ext: 'zip', format: 'lsr', per_layer: false, with_ramps: false },
{ id: S_filter_lsr_layers, name_key: 'filter_lsr_layers', ext: 'zip', format: 'lsr', per_layer: true, with_ramps: false },
{ id: S_filter_cli_single, name_key: 'filter_cli_single', ext: 'zip', format: 'cli', per_layer: false, with_ramps: false },
{ id: S_filter_cli_layers, name_key: 'filter_cli_layers', ext: 'zip', format: 'cli', per_layer: true, with_ramps: false },
{ id: S_filter_3mf_ramps, name_key: 'filter_3mf_ramps', ext: '3mf', format: '3mf', per_layer: false, with_ramps: true },
{ id: S_filter_3mf_edges, name_key: 'filter_3mf_edges', ext: '3mf', format: '3mf', per_layer: false, with_ramps: false }

steps.title: One export, one file
notes: ATU opens the target file and calls exportToFile with the selected filter id. export_to_file refuses to write a package without calculated toolpaths, reads the platform parameters fresh (the laser timing is needed for the LSR time column) and hands over to the writer of the format.

lines: if (!l_filter) return { ok: false, message: 'Unsupported export filter ' + a_filter_id };
// Refuse to write a package without calculated toolpaths.
// Platform parameters may be read in the export (laser timing for the
// LSR time column); part settings come from the model attributes.
let l_ctx = build_export_context(a_model_data, l_platform, a_filter_id, a_progress);
// The 3MF writer needs the attachments BEFORE it writes the package
// (the image is referenced as thumbnail), so they are built here.
// The ZIP formats add them at the end (finish_zip).
// Only reached if S_FILTERS contains a format without a branch above.
return { ok: false, message: 'Unsupported export filter ' + a_filter_id };

steps.title: Every path becomes a PathRecord
notes: All three writers read the layer the same way: read_layer_paths walks the exposure in processing order, so the file keeps the order in which the machine exposes the paths.

Every path becomes a record with its parameter set (BSID), laser, speed, focus, coordinates and one power per edge. The power optimization writes a power per point; if any edge differs from the nominal power, has_power_variation lets the writers switch from the short constant form to the long form.

lines: // Remember if any edge differs from the nominal power, so the
// writers can use the short "constant power" form otherwise.
l_edges.push({ a: l_a, b: l_b, power: l_p });
// Only closed paths can be inner loops (contours around holes).

steps.title: LSR: one line per vector
notes: make_record_lines writes power, direction, start and end point, focus, speed and the start time. Every number goes through fmt: 9 significant digits without trailing zeros. Point powers come from ATU as 32-bit floats, so 150.6 W shows up as 150.600006.
In a single file the clock runs on from layer to layer; in a file per layer reset_time starts every file at 0.

lines: // Values that are the same for every line of the record are formatted once.
// The start time of this vector includes the jump to its start point.
a_state.t_s += MATH.dist(l_x0, l_y0, l_x1, l_y1) / l_speed;
// A hatch line is a vector of its own; a polyline is one vector.

steps.title: CLI+: parameters before every path
notes: Before every record CLI+ writes the parameter set, the laser (counted from 1), power, speed and focus, so every record can be read on its own.

$$POWERS only appears when the power changes along the path. It gets a new pair only where the power, rounded to 0.1 W, changes: with segment splitting the hatch of the explainer gets one pair per piece.

steps.title: CLI+: hatches and polylines
notes: A hatch record is one $$HATCHES line with the label of the part, the number of vectors and their coordinates. A contour is a $$POLYLINE: direction 1 for an outer loop, 0 for a hole, 2 for an open path. A closed contour repeats its first point, as the CLI format requires.
write_layer writes the $$LAYER line even for an empty layer, so the count matches $$LAYERS in the header.

lines: for (let i = 0; i < l_n; ++i) l_v.push(c(l_c[2 * i]), c(l_c[2 * i + 1]));
let l_already_closed = MATH.dist(l_c[0], l_c[1], l_c[2 * (l_n - 1)], l_c[2 * (l_n - 1) + 1]) < S_SAME_POINT_TOL;
// Append the first point again and count it.
let l_geom = (l_rec.kind === 'hatch') ? make_hatches_line(l_rec, l_label) : make_polyline_line(l_rec, l_label);

steps.title: 3MF: power factors and ramps
notes: 3MF stores the power as a factor of the maximum power of the profile. Every path becomes exactly one segment, and the factors sit on its children, as the toolpath specification requires: f on every <hatch> line, and on every <point> the factor of the line it closes.

With ramps, compute_hatch_ramp_powers gives two hatch lines that touch and point the same way the mean power at their common point; they get f1 and f2. The micro vectors of segment splitting touch, so the power runs from piece to piece; separate hatch lines do not touch and keep their own power. Without segment splitting nothing touches, and the two 3MF filters write the same file.

lines: if (!edges_touch(a_rec, k - 1, k) || !edges_collinear(a_rec, k - 1, k)) continue;
r_body.push(hatch_element(a_rec, k, make_factor(l_p0, a_max), make_factor(l_p1, a_max)));
if (a_rec.kind === 'hatch') return { type: 'hatch', body: hatch_body(a_rec, a_max, a_with_ramps) };
// A loop needs at least 3 points; a shorter closed path is written as polyline.
if ((a_rec.kind === 'closed') && (a_rec.edges.length >= 3)) return { type: 'loop', body: loop_body(a_rec, a_max) };

steps.title: What else goes into the package
notes: Every package gets the build job image (a top view of the plate), the platform parameters, the parameters of every part and export_info.json. With these files an exported job can be traced back to the settings it was made with.

The estimated exposure time in export_info.json is the sum the post-processing stored on the tray; for the power wedge of the video it is 280.57 s, and the time column of the LSR adds up to the same value.

recipes.title: LSR powers rounded to 0.1 W
recipes.why: The 9 digits of the LSR also show the float noise of the power (150.600006 W). Rounding like CLI+ does makes the file shorter and easier to read.
recipes.result: Every power in the LSR has at most one decimal. The geometry and the time column do not change.

recipes.title: CLI+ coordinates in micrometers
recipes.why: 5 decimals are 10 nm, far below what a scanner can reach. With 3 decimals (1 µm) every coordinate is two characters shorter.
recipes.result: All $$HATCHES and $$POLYLINE coordinates have 3 decimals. Compare the size of toolpath.cli with the package from before.

recipes.title: Stronger ZIP compression
recipes.why: Text compresses well. Level 9 makes the LSR and CLI+ packages a bit smaller and the export a bit slower; the files inside stay the same.
recipes.result: The ZIP packages are written with the strongest compression. The content of every entry is unchanged.
